## What belongs where?

| Content | Canonical home | Portal role |
|---|---|---|
| Function/API reference | Package documentation | Link and discovery |
| Installation | Package documentation + package landing page | Summarize and link |
| Single-package tutorial | Portal or package docs | Prefer portal when broadly useful |
| Cross-package workflow | Portal | Canonical home |
| Workshop | Portal | Canonical home |
| Release notes | Package repository/site | Link only |
| FAQ | Package or shared support page | Keep close to issue ownership |

## Content front matter

Every tutorial should use consistent metadata so Quarto listings can discover and filter it:

```yaml
---
title: "Process DArTag MADC data to an analysis-ready VCF"
description: "Filter targeted sequencing data, call dosage, and write a sorted VCF."
categories: [BIGr, DArTag, VCF, Genotype processing]
level: intermediate
time: "45 min"
order: 20
---
```

## Tutorial writing pattern

### 1. Goal

State the outcome in biological or analytical terms.

### 2. What you need

List required files, versions, expected columns, and approximate compute needs.

### 3. Workflow map

Show the sequence of steps before introducing code.

### 4. Reproducible steps

Use executable code where feasible. Keep incidental output hidden and preserve outputs that teach interpretation.

### 5. Checkpoint

After each major stage, show what a successful result looks like.

### 6. Troubleshooting

Document common failure modes and the diagnostic information users should collect before filing an issue.

### 7. Next steps

Link to the next workflow rather than ending at a package boundary.

## Migration principle

Do not copy reference material into multiple places. Migrate durable teaching content, then link back to the package's canonical reference documentation. Redirect old URLs when pages move so existing workshop handouts and publications do not break.
